page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a compute-focused instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory is sized at 16.0 GB, which aligns to 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage and does not feature GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal that the AMD microarchitecture yields strong single-core performance, where stress-ng single-core processing achieves 2923.69, placing it in the top 25% tier. Hardware cryptography extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI assist in maintaining average encryption scores in PassMark testing. However, parallel throughput metrics, such as multi-core stress-ng (5862.86) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (23.0 GB/sec), sit in the lower quartile due to the 4-vCPU hardware envelope. Memory operations register average performance on large block read and write benchmarks at 51.54 GB/sec and 38.79 GB/sec respectively.

Without integrated local disks, persistent storage depends on network-attached storage options. The c2d-standard-4 offers reliable dedicated compute threads suited for single-threaded batch execution, lightweight web serving, continuous integration runners, and application hosting workloads that do not demand expansive multi-core parallelism or high-density local database storage.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is an instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of memory, and 32 MB of L3 cache. There are no local storage drives and no hardware accelerators bundled with this server type. Empirical benchmark results highlight strong single-core execution speed, ranking in the upper quartile for single-core stress-ng calculations. Memory bandwidth across large block reads and writes falls within the average range, while aggregate multi-core metrics, database operations, and static web serving throughput are constrained by the 4-vCPU resource limit. The c2d-standard-4 is functionally configured for workloads that prioritize predictable single-thread CPU performance over large-scale parallel capacity, including CI/CD build agents, light web applications, and utility batch jobs.
